help.title: Help
help.faq.addROMs.q: How do I add ROMs to my library?
help.faq.addROMs.a: Drag and drop ROM files onto the app, or use Shift+Cmd+O to select a folder. Supported archive formats (.zip, .7z, .rar) are extracted automatically. You can manage your library folders and rescan from the Library settings page.
help.faq.cores.q: What are cores and how do I install them?
help.faq.cores.a: Cores are emulator engines (based on libretro) that run the games. Each system has a recommended core that is auto-selected when you launch a game. Download cores and optional BIOS files from the Cores settings page.
help.faq.controllers.q: How do I set up a game controller?
help.faq.controllers.a: Connect your controller via USB or Bluetooth — it will be detected automatically. Up to 4 players are supported. Customize button mappings per player and per controller model in the Controllers settings page.
help.faq.saveStates.a: Use Cmd+S (or F5) to save and Cmd+L (or F7) to load. Switch between 10 save slots with Cmd+0–9. Enable auto-save on exit, auto-load on start, and progressive saves from the Saves settings page. Note: save states are disabled during RetroAchievements hardcore mode.
help.faq.shaders.q: What are shaders and how do I use them?
help.faq.shaders.a: Shaders apply visual effects to the game screen — CRT scanlines, LCD grid patterns, or smoothing filters. There are 12 built-in presets across 5 categories (CRT, LCD, Smoothing, Composite, Custom), each with tweakable parameters. Shaders are recommended per system. You can also save custom presets as .truchishader files. Configure shaders from the Display settings page.
help.faq.cheats.a: Download cheat files from the Cheats settings page — you can download all at once, per system, or per game. Once downloaded, toggle cheats on/off from the in-game toolbar. Supported formats: raw hex, Game Genie, Pro Action Replay, and GameShark. Cheats are disabled during RetroAchievements hardcore mode.
help.faq.bezels.a: Bezels are decorative overlays that frame the game screen, simulating a CRT monitor or arcade cabinet. TruchiEmu auto-matches bezels from the Bezel Project repository to your games. You can also import custom bezel images per game. Configure auto-matching and defaults from the Bezels settings page.
help.faq.achievements.a: Sign in with your RetroAchievements Web API key in the RetroAchievements settings page. Achievements unlock automatically during gameplay. Enable hardcore mode for legitimate play — this disables save states, rewind, slow motion, and cheats while hardcore is active.
help.faq.hotkeys.q: How do I customize keyboard shortcuts?
help.faq.hotkeys.a: In-game hotkeys like save/load state, slot selection, input capture, and training mode can be remapped with custom key combinations. Each action supports a primary and secondary binding. Conflict detection warns you if two actions share the same shortcut. Configure hotkeys from the Hotkeys settings page.
help.faq.boxArt.q: How do I change box art or download covers?
help.faq.boxArt.a: Box art is downloaded automatically from Libretro CDN or ScreenScraper when you add games. You can bulk-download or re-download art from the photo.stack toolbar button, or pick a specific image per game from its game info page. Three display styles are available: vertical (3:4), square (1:1), and landscape (4:3). Configure art sources and priority from the Box Art settings page.
help.faq.moveLists.q: What are move lists and how do I use them?
help.faq.moveLists.a: Move lists display fighting game inputs and frame data during gameplay. Data is auto-matched for supported arcade games. You can import custom game data as JSON files. The in-game overlay shows moves, hit levels, and combos per character. Configure visibility and favorites from the Move Lists settings page.
help.faq.inputCapture.q: How do I capture mouse and keyboard input in games?
help.faq.inputCapture.a: Some games (like DOS or ScummVM) need direct mouse and keyboard control. Press Cmd+M (or the configured hotkey) to capture input — your cursor is hidden and all input goes to the game. Press Esc to release capture. This requires macOS Accessibility permissions — grant access in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility.
help.quickStart.addROMs: Add ROMs — Drag and drop game files onto the app, or use Shift+Cmd+O to select a ROM folder.
help.quickStart.downloadCore: Download a Core — Go to Settings > Cores and download the emulator core for your system.
help.quickStart.launchGame: Launch a Game — Double-click any game in your library to start playing.
help.quickStart.customize: Customize — Configure controllers, shaders, bezels, and more in Settings.

hotkeys.explainerBody: Each action can be bound to two keyboard shortcuts (primary + secondary) and one controller button. The controller button popup lists two sources: Apple Controller (gamepads connected via Apple's GameController framework, e.g. Xbox/PS/DualSense) and SDL Controller (gamepads detected via SDL2, used as a fallback for older or third-party controllers). Click the popup to switch sources, then press a button on the controller to capture it.
